summary: Adds a new published CLI/library, @cipherstash/stack-forge (`stash-forge install` / `push`), plus an additive `getEncryptConfig()` on the @cipherstash/stack EncryptionClient and a changesets option. The SDK change is low risk. The risk is in what the new CLI does to customer databases. `push` deactivates every eql_v2_configuration row and then inserts the new one as two autocommit statements with no transaction; the config it inserts can hold cast_as values ('number', 'bigint', 'json') that the EQL 2.1.8 CHECK constraint rejects. In that case the database is left with no active encryption configuration, and any in-flight pending/encrypting migration has also been clobbered. `install` downloads and executes the unpinned `releases/latest` EQL SQL, with no integrity check and usually as a superuser, while the repo itself pins EQL 2.1.8. Its `--force` path re-runs a script that begins with `DROP SCHEMA eql_v2 CASCADE`, which can silently drop indexes and constraints on encrypted columns. Tests mock pg and fetch, and push has no tests at all. Verification needed before release: a transactional push tested against a real EQL database, and a pinned install source.

behaviour_changes.description: New `stash-forge push` command writes to customer databases: it runs `UPDATE eql_v2_configuration SET state = 'inactive'` (all rows, no WHERE) and then a separate `INSERT ... VALUES ('active', $1)` with the encrypt config built by the user's EncryptionClient. It runs on a plain pg.Client with no BEGIN/COMMIT, and it bypasses EQL's pending -> encrypting -> active lifecycle functions.

New `stash-forge install` command downloads the EQL install SQL from GitHub `releases/latest` (plain or Supabase variant) at run time and executes it against the configured database inside a transaction. With `--supabase` it also grants anon/authenticated/service_role access to the eql_v2 schema and alters default privileges for role postgres. `--drizzle` writes the same downloaded SQL into a drizzle-kit custom migration file.

The installed-check is only the existence of the eql_v2 schema. `--force` (which the CLI suggests when EQL is already installed) re-runs the full install script, which in the repo's vendored EQL 2.1.8 starts with `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v2 CASCADE`.
@cipherstash/stack EncryptionClient gains a public `getEncryptConfig()` method that returns the validated encrypt config (additive; minor changeset).

New published package @cipherstash/stack-forge (public access, ESM+CJS library entry, ESM `stash-forge` bin, node >=22) with runtime deps pg, jiti, zod, dotenv, @clack/prompts. `push` loads the user's TypeScript config and encryption client via jiti, which executes the module, and the example client awaits `Encryption()` at top level.
The changesets config enables the experimental `onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange` option, which changes how versions are bumped for peer dependents in every future release from this monorepo.

Ships a README and an agent skill (skills/stash-forge/SKILL.md) describing push and install. The README says the runtime @cipherstash/stack reads the active configuration from eql_v2_configuration, but the SDK uses its own in-process config.

failure_scenarios.title: push leaves the database with no active EQL configuration when the insert fails
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs `stash-forge push` with a schema containing a column whose cast_as is not in EQL's allowed set. Examples are `.dataType('number')`, `.dataType('bigint')`, `.dataType('json')` and any `.searchableJson()` column (cast_as 'json'). Any other INSERT error (constraint, permission, dropped connection) also triggers it.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: push.ts:32-43 runs `UPDATE eql_v2_configuration SET state = 'inactive'` and then the INSERT as two separate autocommit queries, with no BEGIN. The stack schema builder emits cast_as values 'number', 'bigint' and 'json' unchanged (schema/index.ts:26-28, 339-344). The EQL 2.1.8 CHECK constraint (config_check_cast) only accepts text, int, small_int, big_int, real, double, boolean, date and jsonb, and RAISEs on anything else (sql:3598-3613, 3642-3650). The INSERT fails after the UPDATE has already committed. Because the UPDATE has no WHERE clause, it also flips any 'pending' or 'encrypting' row to inactive, bypassing EQL's migrate/activate lifecycle.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The previously active configuration is deactivated and nothing replaces it. Anything that reads the active config, such as EQL config functions and likely CipherStash Proxy, loses its encryption configuration. In-progress encryption migrations are silently abandoned. The CLI reports the INSERT error, but the destructive half has already been applied, and recovery means manually reactivating a row.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Wrap the UPDATE and INSERT in a single transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT, ROLLBACK on error). Restrict the UPDATE to state = 'active', or use EQL's own config functions. Map stack cast_as values to EQL names before inserting, or validate the config against EQL's rules before touching the table.

failure_scenarios.title: install --force drops EQL-dependent indexes and constraints on encrypted columns
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user with EQL already installed and tables using eql_v2_encrypted columns with EQL indexes or constraints runs `stash-forge install --force`, as the CLI itself suggests when EQL is already installed.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: install.ts:70-80 skips the installed-check only under --force and prints 'Use --force to re-run the install script.' The executed script (vendored 2.1.8, sql:1-2) begins `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v2 CASCADE`. That CASCADE removes every object depending on eql_v2 functions, operators and operator classes, for example check constraints added by eql_v2.add_encrypted_constraint (sql:183-189) and indexes using eql_v2.encrypted_operator_class (sql:2239-2247). The script recreates the schema but not the user's dependent objects. The installer comment calls the script 'idempotent and safe to re-run' (installer/index.ts:174).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Encrypted columns lose their indexes and check constraints without an error. Queries keep working but slow down, and invalid payloads are no longer rejected. Nothing tells the user; the install reports 'Done!'.

failure_scenarios.title: install executes an unpinned, unverified 'latest' EQL SQL bundle as a privileged role
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs `stash-forge install` (or `--drizzle`) after a new EQL release that is incompatible with the installed @cipherstash/stack version, or while the release asset has been tampered with or replaced.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Both installer/index.ts:3-6 and install.ts:242-262 fetch `releases/latest/download/...sql` with no version pin and no checksum or signature check. The SQL is executed directly (installer/index.ts:201-202), usually by a superuser, since checkPermissions steers users there, or it is written into a committed Drizzle migration. The repo itself pins EQL 2.1.8 (packages/schema/cipherstash-encrypt-2-1-8.sql), so the client/SQL pairing that stack was tested against is not what forge installs.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Installs can't be reproduced, and the version is chosen by the release date rather than by the user. A future EQL major or minor change to payload/search-term handling can install SQL functions that do not match the client's search terms, so queries return wrong or empty results. A compromised release asset becomes arbitrary SQL run as superuser on customer databases.

failure_scenarios.title: A positional argument after --dry-run silently disables the dry run
failure_scenarios.trigger: The user runs e.g. `stash-forge install --dry-run foo` or `stash-forge push --dry-run x`, or a script appends an argument after a boolean flag.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: parseArgs (bin/stash-forge.ts:39-55) treats any non-`--` token after a flag as that flag's value. `--dry-run foo` sets values['dry-run'] = 'foo' and leaves flags['dry-run'] undefined, so installCommand/pushCommand run for real.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A command the user meant as a preview modifies the database: it runs the EQL install or the push from FS-1.
missing_verification: Unit tests for parseArgs with boolean flags followed by positional tokens
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Declare which options take values (name, out). Treat all others as boolean, or use node:util parseArgs with an explicit option schema.

evidence.claim: push connects, runs UPDATE eql_v2_configuration SET state='inactive' (no WHERE), then a separate INSERT ... ('active', $1). No BEGIN/COMMIT; pg.Client autocommits each statement.
castAsEnum allows 'bigint', 'boolean', 'date', 'number', 'string', 'json', 'text'.
build() maps only 'string' to 'text'; 'number', 'bigint' and 'json' (set by searchableJson) pass through unchanged into the encrypt config.
EQL 2.1.8 config_check_cast accepts only text, int, small_int, big_int, real, double, boolean, date, jsonb and RAISEs otherwise.
eql_v2_configuration_data_check CHECK constraint applies config_check_cast to every row's data.
EQL keeps unique active/pending/encrypting states and manages transitions with its own functions (e.g. lines 3380-3394 move pending->encrypting->active).
Install URLs point to releases/latest for both the standard and the Supabase SQL, with no version pin.
The Drizzle path downloads releases/latest SQL with no integrity check and writes it into a migration file.
install() downloads the script and executes it in BEGIN/COMMIT; with supabase it also runs grants; there is no checksum or version check.
EQL 2.1.8 install script begins with DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v2 CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA eql_v2.

eql_v2.add_encrypted_constraint adds table CHECK constraints that call eql_v2 functions; operator classes on eql_v2_encrypted are defined in eql_v2 (lines 2239-2247). Both depend on the schema that CASCADE drops.
The installed-check is skipped only without --force; the CLI suggests 'Use --force to re-run the install script.'
Installer tests mock pg.Client and global fetch; they assert permission logic, schema-exists checks, BEGIN/COMMIT and ROLLBACK, and that the URL contains cipherstash-encrypt.sql.
Config tests cover loadStashConfig only (missing file, invalid, valid); loadEncryptConfig is not tested.
